ledger.x: c. 1100 BCE: the Greek world enters the Dark Age. Infobox 'c. 1180-800 BC'; 'Mycenaean palaces began to come to an end around 1200 BC', with revolts 'c. 1200-1150 BC' and the fall 'attributed to a Dorian or Sea Peoples invasion'. Cliopatria's -1100 start is kept as the handover from Mycenaean Greece, whose page ends…

c. 1000 BCE: Greeks from the mainland settle the Anatolian coast. The page's 'early movement from mainland Greece to the Anatolian coast' is dated 'perhaps as early as 1000 BC'; it names no cities, so the gazetteer's Ionia stands for the coast. Cliopatria's shape drops Anatolia at this date instead; the keyframe is…

c. 1000 BCE: Greek-speaking Cyprus is drawn with the Greek world on Cliopatria's date. The page: Greek speakers arrived 'in the late 13th to 11th centuries BC, but did not colonize the island'; 'sub-Mycenaean Cyprus (c. 1100-1050 BC)'; the Dorian invasion page notes the Arcadocypriot features shared by 'Arcadia in the…

c. 800 BCE: the Dark Age ends and the age of the poleis begins. The period ends 'in the beginning of the Protohistoric Iron Age, c. 800 BC'; the oikoi are 'the origins of the later poleis'; 'By the beginning of 8th century BC, a new Greek alphabet system was adopted from the Phoenician alphabet'; 'the first Olympics…

certainty.note: No borders at all: the row is an archaeological period, drawn as the area of Greek settlement; the Anatolian coast and Cyprus are the softest, the Aegean coastlines sharp by nature.
